title: Only borrow interest above the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is passed to stUSDS lenders
content:
The spread term in A.4.4.1.3.2 is not the borrow rate but the borrow rate *minus a floor*: `(SKY Borrow Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) * Utilization`. A.4.4.1.3.2.1.3 confirms `SKY Borrow Minimum Rate` is a separately governed parameter defined at A.4.4.1.3.5.2.

The non-obvious consequence: borrowers pay the full SKY Borrow Rate, but lenders are only credited the portion above the minimum. The minimum-rate slice never reaches stUSDS holders. It is a protocol take-rate expressed as a floor rather than as an explicit fee percentage.

Encoding the fee this way has a specific property. A percentage cut scales with the borrow rate, so the protocol earns most when credit is expensive. A fixed floor does the opposite — it is the *first* claim on interest, fully collected even in a low-rate regime, and its relative weight shrinks as the borrow rate climbs. The protocol's revenue from this facility is therefore stable in absolute terms while lender yield captures the upside of rate spikes.

At the boundary case, if the SKY Borrow Rate is set at or near the minimum, the entire spread term collapses to zero and stUSDS holders earn the Sky Savings Rate less the `Rfactor` deduction — potentially *below* what plain sUSDS would pay, while carrying lending and liquidity risk. Whether stUSDS is attractive is therefore a direct function of how far governance sets the borrow rate above the minimum, which makes that gap the key parameter for anyone evaluating the position.
description: Because the formula uses (SKY Borrow Rate − SKY Borrow Minimum Rate), the minimum-rate portion of every borrower's payment is retained by the system rather than distributed as lender yield.
